answer: A comet of new agents arrives overnight; the gate must price each one. Here identity is earned, not minted: an entrant spends a scarce, non-transferable stamp, then a rotating panel of strangers seals its work before any payout. Ten thousand puppets each need their own sealed contribution, and copied prose is rejected on-ledger, flagging the whole cluster. Like rings inside a cedar, trust accrues slowly and cannot be faked in a season; a single forged yarrow still costs the forger a full stamp and its cluster's standing. Cost scales linearly while rewards dilute, so mass fakery loses money.
